text:
Alex C (Support): FYI incoming escalation from Acme — SSO started failing right after their IdP cert rollover earlier today. They report 400 on ACS POST, users hit the app login and get redirected back with an error page. Raised ticket #ACME-455.
Priya R (SRE): @Alex can you paste the SAML response/relaystate logs and the ACS URL they're using? Also any assertion error text would help.
Alex C (Support): From the customer's side: 
```
Status: 400 Bad Request\nEndpoint: https://app.redwood.example/sso/acs\nRequest payload: SAMLResponse=... (base64)\nError shown: "SAML response signature invalid"\n```
They said this worked until the IdP rotated certs at 06:12 UTC. They also sent a chunk of their IdP metadata (trimmed):
```
<EntityDescriptor entityID="https://idp.acme.example">
  <IDPSSODescriptor>
    <KeyDescriptor use="signing">
      <KeyInfo>...X509Certificate (new cert) ...</KeyInfo>
    </KeyDescriptor>
    <KeyDescriptor use="encryption">
      <KeyInfo>...X509Certificate (old cert) ...</KeyInfo>
    </KeyDescriptor>
    <SingleSignOnService Binding="urn:oasis:names:tc:SAML:2.0:bindings:HTTP-POST" Location="https://idp.acme.example/sso/POST"/>
  </IDPSSODescriptor>
</EntityDescriptor>
```
Alex C (Support): They also mentioned their ACS URL in the IdP config uses a trailing slash: `https://app.redwood.example/sso/acs/` (customer portal shows with slash) while our route is `https://app.redwood.example/sso/acs` (no slash). Could be important.
Priya R (SRE): Two quick possibilities: 1) the IdP metadata's KeyDescriptor order means our metadata parser picks the wrong key for signature validation, or 2) the cert chain/chain-intermediate isn't provided so signature verification fails. Trailing slash mismatch can surface as unexpected audience/ACS mismatch if the SP config compares exact URLs.
Mike T (Platform Eng): Can you capture the raw SAMLResponse that failed so we can validate signature locally and see which cert signed it? If they rotated, the signature might be from the new cert while our stored metadata still points to the old public cert OR the IdP uploaded only leaf cert and omitted intermediate CA.
Alex C (Support): Customer uploaded the SAMLResponse (base64). I decoded and ran `xmlsec1 --verify` on it; output shows:
```
ERROR: failed to verify: X509 PKIX verification error: unable to get local issuer certificate
```
But the assertion signature header points to the new cert's fingerprint.
Priya R (SRE): That error strongly suggests the IdP didn't include the full chain in the metadata X509Certificate element (or it's not trusted by our cert store). Two quick checks: ask them for the full cert chain (leaf + intermediates) or have them export metadata again with full chain. Also ask them to check the KeyDescriptor ordering — we prefer signing KeyDescriptor first.
Mike T (Platform Eng): Also check our SP config for strict ACS URL matching. If the IdP is posting to `.../acs/` vs `.../acs` sometimes frameworks normalize but our middleware doesn't. If the Audience or Recipient contains the trailing slash variant, validation fails. Quick workaround: temporarily add the trailing-slash variant to allowed ACS URLs for that tenant.
Alex C (Support): I asked the customer to: 1) re-export IdP metadata including the full certificate chain, 2) confirm which certificate is used for signing now, and 3) temporarily post to the exact ACS path without the trailing slash (they said they can update their binding).
saml-bot: New message from test validator: Received SAMLResponse sample, running automated checks...
saml-bot: Check results: signature present, signing cert subject CN=acme-idp.example, fingerprint=AB:CD:EF:..., chain incomplete (missing intermediate CA), KeyDescriptor order: signing then encryption (OK) — NOTE: metadata showed old cert in encryption slot in some versions.
Priya R (SRE): Good data from the bot — chain incomplete is the main lead. Alex, do we have logs showing `AudienceRestriction`/`Recipient` mismatch?
Alex C (Support): From our SP debug logs when validating: `Recipient mismatch: expected https://app.redwood.example/sso/acs, got https://app.redwood.example/sso/acs/` (we log both exact values).
Mike T (Platform Eng): So two distinct failures: cert chain and ACS trailing slash. Prioritize chain first (signature verification). For ACS mismatch, we'll relax strict check for that tenant for now and add the exact trailing-slash variant to allowed recipients. I'll open a quick PR to allow multiple ACS variants per tenant mapping.
Priya R (SRE): Steps to resolution:(1) Customer re-exports metadata with full chain and confirms signing cert fingerprint. (2) We temporarily add `https://app.redwood.example/sso/acs/` to tenant's allowed ACS list and redeploy small config change (no code change). (3) After they confirm successful logins, we ask them to publish metadata with the full chain and correct key ordering.
Alex C (Support): Customer replied: they re-exported metadata — includes full chain now and signing cert fingerprint matches new cert. They also updated the IdP to post to exact ACS (no trailing slash). They confirm some users could login but a handful still fail.
Priya R (SRE): For the stragglers: check browser caches and SLOs — some sessions may have cookies tied to older SAML flows. Ask those users to clear site cookies or try incognito. Also check our logs for any remaining signature failures.
Alex C (Support): After updating our tenant allowed ACS list and them re-uploading metadata with chain, we saw successful xmlsec verification in logs: `xmlsec verify: OK (signature valid)` and `SAML login successful, user: j.smith@acme.example`.
Mike T (Platform Eng): I pushed the temporary ACS variant to the tenant mapping and added a note to infra runbook: when onboarding IdPs, require full cert chain in metadata and document that our ACS matching is strict about trailing slash; we will improve normalization later but this is lowest risk.
Alex C (Support): Customer confirmed resolved at 15:37 UTC — they rotated back to stable cert and then uploaded full chain; logins are green. They're going to coordinate with their IdP team to ensure future rotations include intermediate CA in metadata and to avoid swapping signing/encryption descriptors.
Priya R (SRE): Closing notes: root cause = incomplete cert chain in IdP metadata (xmlsec couldn't verify up to trusted root) plus ACS URL exact-match mismatch (trailing slash). Remediation = upload full chain + add temporary ACS variant on SP side. Follow-up: add metadata validation check on upload that flags incomplete chain and suggest ordering for KeyDescriptor.
Alex C (Support): Thanks all. I'll update ticket #ACME-455 and include steps we took and recommended guardrails. :white_check_mark:
Mike T (Platform Eng): I'll add the runbook and a small validator task to the backlog (PLAT-1429).
Priya R (SRE): Marking thread resolved. :thumbsup:
